 Editor's Pick Spotlight 
 FREDERICK COUNTY REWIND: Thanksgiving’s Frederick roots 
 By James Rada Jr.
Special to The News-Post 
 Nov 14, 2026 
 4 hrs ago 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 WhatsApp 
 SMS 
 Email 
 John Hanson's Thanksgiving Day proclamation. 
 Library of Congress

 While the Pilgrims and the Wampanoag people are commonly associated with the first Thanksgiving feast in 1621, they weren’t the ones who turned it into a national holiday. The holiday we celebrate each November went through several iterations, and Frederick’s John Hanson played a role in one of its early national observances.
 When news arrived at the Continental Congress that British Gen. Charles Cornwallis had surrendered at Yorktown in October 1781, there was celebration and relief. The surrender meant that, for all intents and purposes, the American Revolution was nearing its end. However, hostilities continued as the Americans awaited word from England about its response to Cornwallis’ surrender.
